passage: My name is Vijay, and for three weeks I crossed the corridor to avoid Professor Sarita's room. Everyone said she failed people for fun. My thermodynamics assignment was half done and I could not understand the second question, yet my stomach turned every time I saw her door. Finally I wrote down three specific doubts, read the chapter again, and went during office hours with sweaty palms. She looked up, said "Sit," and asked me to show my working. I expected a scolding. Instead she circled one line and said, "Good start, wrong sign here." Ten minutes. I walked out lighter, almost laughing. She still scares me a little, but now I know she forgets her glasses on her forehead.

qa.q: How many specific doubts did Vijay write down before going?
qa.a: He wrote down three specific doubts.

qa.q: Why did Vijay's stomach turn every time he saw her door?
qa.a: He was scared of her strictness, having heard she failed people, and feared a scolding about his half done assignment.

qa.q: What would you advise Vijay to do if he gets stuck again?
qa.a: Go early to office hours again with specific doubts and his own working, instead of avoiding her until the problem grows.

qa.q: How might Professor Sarita see a student turning up at office hours?
qa.a: She probably sees a student who wants to learn; her calm "Sit" and quick correction suggest she is glad to help, not eager to scold.

grounding: A student afraid of a strict professor prepares, attends office hours and finds her more approachable.

passage:
By the fourth week of the semester I hadn't understood a single lecture in Dr. Nitin Sharma's Control Systems, and I'd done the worst possible thing: nothing. He had a reputation for sending students out over late assignments, so I skipped his office hours and hoped it would click on its own. It didn't. My first quiz came back at 4 out of 20.
That scared me more than he did. So on Monday I wrote down exactly where I was stuck, three examples, page numbers, and went at 4 p.m.
He was eating a banana. He had a small plant on his desk and a photo of a dog. He listened, drew one diagram, and said, "Everyone gets lost at transfer functions. Come every Monday until you don't."
I've gone five Mondays now. I got 14 on the second quiz. He's still strict. He's also a person who named his dog Resistor.
— Vikas

qa.q: What did Vikas score on the first quiz?
Why did Vikas avoid Dr. Sharma's office hours at first?
qa.a: Vikas was scared of Dr. Sharma's strict reputation and hoped the subject would click without help.

qa.q: What did Vikas do to make the visit work?
qa.a: Wrote down exactly where the confusion was, with three examples and page numbers, and went to office hours on Monday.

qa.q: How does Dr. Sharma see Vikas's struggle?
qa.a: As normal ("Everyone gets lost at transfer functions"), and he invites Vikas to come every Monday.

grounding: Shows fear of a strict professor, the cost of avoiding him, and preparing, going to office hours and finding him human.

passage:
Academic advisor's note, MSc first year, 11 October
Neelam has missed two thesis check-ins with Prof. Vinita Kulkarni. Today she came to me instead, pale, saying she was "too scared to face her now" because the delay had grown so long. She admitted she had been avoiding the department corridor for three weeks.
I asked what she was afraid of. "That she'll say I'm not serious." I pointed out that each missed week made that more likely, not less.
We prepared together: a one-page summary of what she had done, where she was stuck, and a realistic new timeline. I suggested she open with an apology, not excuses.
At 3 p.m. I walked with her as far as the professor's door and waited in the corridor. She came out twenty minutes later, flushed but smiling. "She said, 'Next time, come when you're stuck, not when you've finished being scared.'" They have fixed weekly Tuesday meetings.

qa.q: How many thesis check-ins had Neelam missed?

qa.a: That Prof. Kulkarni would think she wasn't serious; she was pale and too scared to face her.

qa.q: How did the advisor help Neelam face the professor?
qa.a: By preparing a one-page summary, stuck points and a new timeline with her, suggesting an apology instead of excuses, and walking her to the door.

qa.q: How does Prof. Kulkarni respond to Neelam?
qa.a: Firmly but kindly, telling her to come when stuck and setting weekly Tuesday meetings.

grounding: Illustrates avoiding a strict professor until the problem grows, and preparing and going to see her with support.
